learning_objective: The learner will calculate the mean gain of each group, the difference of means, and the median gain of each group from a table of 24 gains, and decide whether the difference meets the 5-point threshold, with at least 5 of 6 answers correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** mean-difference-calculator
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the mean gain of each group, the difference of means, and the median gain of each group from a table of 24 gains, and decide whether the difference meets the 5-point threshold, with at least 5 of 6 answers correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Mean Score, Difference of Means, Learning Gain (defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 16). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers six questions. An answer is correct when it matches the Correct answer column in Content. Numeric answers are correct to one decimal place. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Sorting the gains or using a calculator inside the sim is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The mean and the median are the same number. (2) A positive difference always meets the hypothesis. (3) The mean of post-test scores can replace the mean of gains. **Instructional Rationale:** Calculating means and a difference from raw data is an Apply-level action that the learner will repeat on a real test. Twelve values per group are few enough to calculate by hand and enough to need a method. **Content:** The data, shown at all times (learning gains in percentage points, made up for the Watershed Basics pilot): | Group | The twelve gains, in the order of student code | |---|---| | Control (original version) | 20, 15, 8, 19, 18, 17, 21, 10, 18, 9, 3, 22 | | Treatment (improved version) | 31, 11, 20, 33, 23, 26, 18, 28, 9, 18, 27, 20 | The hypothesis, shown at all times: the treatment group's mean gain will be at least 5 percentage points larger than the control group's. The six questions: | # | Question | Answer type | Correct answer | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | What is the mean gain of the control group? | Number to one decimal place | 15.0 | The gains add to 180, and 180 divided by 12 is 15.0. | | 2 | What is the mean gain of the treatment group? | Number to one decimal place | 22.0 | The gains add to 264, and 264 divided by 12 is 22.0. | | 3 | What is the difference of means, treatment minus control? | Number with a sign | +7.0 | 22.0 minus 15.0 is 7.0. | | 4 | Does the difference meet the hypothesis? | Yes or No | Yes | 7.0 >= 5. | | 5 | What is the median gain of the control group? | Number to one decimal place | 17.5 | Sorted, the sixth and seventh gains are 17 and 18, and their middle is 17.5. | | 6 | What is the median gain of the treatment group? | Number to one decimal place | 21.5 | Sorted, the sixth and seventh gains are 20 and 23, and their middle is 21.5. | **Provenance:** The gains are illustrative examples made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The calculations follow the chapter sections "Mean Score" and "Difference of Means". **Rules:** The mean is the sum divided by 12. The median of twelve values is the mean of the sixth and seventh values after sorting. The difference is treatment minus control. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the data and the first question. 2. The learner enters an answer, and the answer is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After question 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 questions in the order of the table, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [answer]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [answer]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can compare two groups." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed question. **Starting State:** The data table, the hypothesis, and question 1. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of group statistics and its difference of means use the same gains.
